summary: The SQS listener passes the message straight to createInvoiceFromProviderEvent with no processed-message check, and the work starts with an insert and then a non-idempotent charge (no idempotency key in the body). If processing fails after the charge (publishEvent or commit), the transaction rolls back the invoice row but the provider charge stands, and a redelivery charges the customer again.

evidence.claim: First side effect is an insert inside the transaction, with no lookup of the incoming event before it.
The provider charge runs before commit, so a rollback after this line leaves the charge in place.
The charge POST carries no idempotency key (body at lines 26-29 has only customer, amount, currency), so a repeated call creates a second charge.
Listener consumes the SQS queue with no message id check before calling the service.
billing_invoice has only a generated primary key; V2 adds no unique index on it, so no business-key constraint stops a duplicate insert.

summary: LedgerSyncService.adjust opens a transaction, saves a posting (holding a pooled connection), then calls LedgerAuditService.record, which is REQUIRES_NEW and needs a second connection. Under load each request can hold one connection while waiting for another, which exhausts the pool. The audit-row intent is visible, but the pool sizing that would cover it is not in the packet.

evidence.claim: The inner method needs its own connection while the caller's transaction is still open.
The outer transaction already holds a connection before the nested call.
The REQUIRES_NEW call is made from inside the open outer transaction, so each request needs two connections at once.

summary: A lookup on the PayPal reference runs before the save, and the paypal_event_id column has a unique constraint in both the entity and V1. A duplicate delivery is skipped by the lookup, and a concurrent duplicate is stopped by the constraint, so no second receipt row is stored. The concurrent duplicate surfaces as an unhandled constraint exception (HTTP 500), which causes provider retries but not duplicate effects.

evidence.claim: The entity maps the reference to a unique column.
The database enforces uniqueness, so a second insert of the same reference fails.
Sequential redeliveries are skipped before the write.

summary: retry loads the invoice without a lock, calls the provider charge, and only then saves the charged state. A commit failure after the charge leaves the invoice uncharged while the charge exists, so the next admin retry charges again. Two concurrent retries both see an uncharged invoice and both charge, since the charge has no idempotency key.

evidence.claim: The invoice is read without a lock or conditional claim, so concurrent retries both see it uncharged.
The charge is made before the charged state is saved, inside the transaction.
The charged state is persisted only after the remote charge, and the save is the last step, so a failed commit leaves the invoice uncharged.
The charge body has no idempotency key, so a repeated charge is not deduplicated by the provider on this path.

summary: LedgerReconciliationJob has no @DisallowConcurrentExecution, so an overlapping run loads the same unsynced postings and marks them again. The repeated write only sets synced_at to a new time and sends nothing, so the harm is redundant work and a rewritten timestamp, not a duplicated business effect; this is a judgement call.

evidence.claim: The job class has no @DisallowConcurrentExecution annotation.
Each overlapping run re-marks the same rows; this is the only write.
A plain save, not a conditional update or row claim, so no row count check stops the second run.
